chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who rides a mount, let him bequeath.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.رَاحِلَةً: a mount or beast of burden used for travel
key_terms.يُوصِ: to make a will or bequest

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on making a will before traveling or going for Hajj?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises that anyone mounting a beast of burden should make a will, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *wasiyyah* as a recommended act (*mustahabb*) to ensure spiritual and material continuity. This hadith underscores the unpredictability of travel and the necessity of settling debts and distributing assets before embarking, a practice deeply rooted in early Islamic jurisprudence to prevent disputes among heirs.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of his men, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who rides his ride (to go for Hajj), so let him bequeath’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ya’qub ibn Yazid from ibn abu ‘Umayr from certain individuals of his people who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that if one rides a means of transportation for al-Hajj, he should make his will.”
